\subsection{Simulation: Replayed Production Sessions}\label{sec:sim}

The simulator replays the production sessions of \S\ref{sec:exp-traces}
against a simulated replica that follows the vLLM~v1 engine's rules.
Every iteration hands a token budget to the running turns in admission
order, one token to each decoding turn and the rest to the prefill at
the head, so prefill runs on the compute the batch leaves, as in
\S\ref{sec:batch}. A waiting turn is admitted at the start of an
iteration once its whole prompt fits; its KV then grows chunk by chunk,
and a growth that does not fit preempts the latest admitted turn. KV is
cached in 16-token blocks and evicted from the tail of a context, so an
evicted turn re-prefills, with the work~\eqref{eq:prefill}, only the
part it lost. A finished session's blocks stay cached, since the engine
cannot tell that the session ended. The workload side is measured and the cost model is the testbed's
(\S\ref{sec:exp-testbed}): the prefill terms of the cost fit and a
decode iteration of $\omega=\simCalOmega$\,s, the inter-token latency
of the lightest long-context replay, which did not vary with the
context ($\beta=0$);
no number here is a measurement of a serving system.
Before the replay, every proposition is checked as a seeded test under
its own assumptions and with one assumption dropped
(Appendix~\ref{app:sim}; \simChecksPassed{} of \simChecks{} checks
pass). Three of those checks matter later. On a replica with vLLM's
engine rules, forced misses land at the upper end of the bracket of
Proposition~\ref{prop:price} and change the number in the decode batch
by at most \simDecodeShiftPct\,\%: a miss's prefill lengthens the
iterations the decoding turns share. On open sessions at the vLLM-rule replica with
the testbed's cost model (Table~\ref{tab:sim-evict-dyn}), the priced
and shortest-first eviction orders are indistinguishable within seed noise.
Least recently used matches them at the lower load and pays
\simEvictLruRatioMax{} times their time to first token at the higher load.
At the higher load, increasing the admission cap reduces the hit rate and
raises time to first token (Table~\ref{tab:sim-admission}). The price needs the end of a session:
when a finished session's blocks stay, as vLLM's engine keeps them, the
byte-second order cannot tell them from a paused session's, and at the
lower load its hit rate falls from \simEndKnownHit{} to
\simEndUnknownHit{} and its time to first token rises
\simEndUnknownTtftRatio{} times. The load at which moving beats
affinity follows $\rho^*$ of~\eqref{eq:rhostar}.

\paragraph{Replayed production sessions.} Table~\ref{tab:sim-trace}
(Appendix~\ref{app:sim}) plays each real session's appends, outputs, think times and length on
the replica; a gap above ten minutes starts a new session whose first
prompt is the accumulated context (Table~\ref{tab:sim-trace-split}
varies the threshold). With no eviction every follow-up turn
hits and its prefill work still has
$\mathrm{CV}^2=\simTraceOpenCvMin$--$\simTraceOpenCvMax$ from the
appends alone, while the mean TTFT of
\simTraceOpenTtftMin--\simTraceOpenTtftMax\,s is set by the cold first
prompts. Once the pool is finite the cap on live sessions binds and
the replica is a closed system of $N$ sessions. At the smaller $N$ of
each pool a follow-up turn reuses on average at least
\simTraceTightReusedMin{} of its reusable prefix, although only a share
of \simTraceTightHitMin{} or more reuses all of it: eviction takes the
tail of a context, so most misses are partial and cheap, and the
hit/miss mixture supplies only
\simTraceTightMixMin--\simTraceTightMixMax\,\% of the variance of
follow-up prefill work. At the larger $N$ the replica thrashes (hit
rate at most \simTraceLooseHitMax, mean TTFT above
\simTraceLooseTtftMin\,s). The PK wait from the measured $\lambda$,
$\E[S]$ and $\E[S^2]$ is above the observed wait in every cell, by
\simTracePkRatioMin{} to \simTracePkRatioMax{} times, as
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite} says it must for exponential work. For
the price itself, Table~\ref{tab:sim-trace-price} forces a share
$\delta$ of follow-up turns to reuse nothing, as a nonce at the head of
the prompt would, and compares the rise of
the number in the prefill stage with the bracket of
Proposition~\ref{prop:price} and with the finite-source price of
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite}. With \simPriceLiveMin{} to
\simPriceLiveMax{} sessions live, the open bracket's lower end
overstates the rise by \simPriceOverMin{} to \simPriceOverMax{} times.
At the higher rate and $\delta=10\,\%$ the added work puts the open
queue past its pole while the capped replica stays finite. The
Markovian finite-source price, which ignores the second moment of the
work, understates the rise by \simPriceFiniteRatioMin{} to
\simPriceFiniteRatioMax{} times. The cap $N-L_P$ holds in
\simPriceCapHolds{} cell.
